purpose: Provides a repo snapshot pipeline that turns repository changes into durable architecture understanding artifacts.
summary: Augur subscribes to repositories, runs deterministic detectors for each commit, and prepares semantic snapshots that explain current architecture, flows, observability, concerns, and reading paths.

system_kinds.label: Event-driven snapshot worker
system_kinds.role: Runs repository analysis from queued commit events.

promises.title: Continuous Repository Snapshots
promises.description: Produce one commit-scoped snapshot artifact set whenever a subscribed repository branch changes.

actors.name: Repository Owner
actors.description: Connects a repository and reads the resulting snapshot history.

actors.name: GitHub Push Webhook
actors.description: Supplies branch push events that identify the current and previous commits.

components.name: Repository Subscription CLI
components.description: Creates a durable subscription for a repository branch and queues the first snapshot job. It is the setup path that lets a user connect a repo once and let the pipeline continue from push events.

relationships.description: Writes the initial snapshot job into the shared queue.

components.name: GitHub Webhook Handler
components.description: Receives push payloads, verifies optional signatures, matches subscribed repositories, and enqueues snapshot jobs. It avoids running analysis inline so GitHub delivery is quick and retryable.

relationships.description: Turns a push event into an augur-job.v1 queue item.

components.name: Snapshot Queue
components.description: Stores pending, running, completed, and failed snapshot jobs in a shared filesystem-backed queue. It is neutral pipeline state rather than website-owned or Augur-owned content.

relationships.description: Hands queued jobs to the worker loop.

components.name: Deterministic Snapshot Worker
components.description: Consumes queued jobs, materializes the requested commit, runs deterministic detectors, and writes commit-scoped artifacts. The semantic agent will later consume those artifacts to produce the final snapshot.json.

relationships.description: Writes detector output, deltas, and semantic snapshot artifacts under the commit output directory.

components.name: Shared Snapshot Store
components.description: Holds commit-scoped artifacts produced by agents and deterministic workers, plus future human edits from the website. It is a shared product artifact boundary, not an implementation detail owned by either side.

flows.name: Subscribe Repository And Run First Snapshot
flows.description: A repository owner adds a repository through the CLI. The subscription is recorded, an initial job is queued, and the worker produces the first commit-scoped artifact set.
flows.trigger: User runs repo add with a repository URL and branch.
flows.outcome: The shared snapshot store contains the first deterministic output directory for the branch head.

steps.action: records subscription and creates an initial job
steps.effect: A pending job exists for the current branch head.

steps.action: hands the job to the worker loop
steps.effect: The worker owns the job attempt.

steps.action: runs detectors on the checked-out commit
steps.effect: Commit artifacts are written under the shared output root.

flows.name: Push Event To Snapshot Artifacts
flows.description: GitHub sends a push payload for a subscribed branch. The webhook enqueues a job and the worker updates the shared artifact store for the new commit.
flows.trigger: GitHub push webhook for a subscribed branch.
flows.outcome: A new commit directory is available for semantic snapshot generation and website browsing.

steps.action: accepts and normalizes the push payload
steps.effect: A queue item identifies the repo, branch, current sha, and previous sha.

steps.action: checks out the current commit and runs detector modules
steps.effect: The commit output directory receives detector output, diff, report, and run metadata.

patterns.name: Event-driven worker pipeline
patterns.summary: Push events and setup commands enqueue jobs, while workers consume them independently and write durable artifacts.

observability.summary: The important operational questions are whether webhook delivery succeeds, whether the queue drains, and whether commit artifacts are produced for each subscribed branch head.

scenarios.title: Snapshot queue stalls
scenarios.description: Jobs remain pending and the website stops seeing newer commit snapshots.

path.trigger: Worker loop is not running or cannot read the queue.
path.outcome: New push events are accepted but no new snapshot artifacts appear.

steps.effect: The worker does not move jobs to done or failed.

measurements.name: pending_jobs
measurements.label: Pending Job Count
measurements.description: Number of jobs in the pending queue.

concerns.title: Semantic stage is not deployed yet
concerns.summary: The deterministic event layer works, but production semantic snapshot writing still needs a deployed agent or SDK worker.

stories.title: How a commit becomes snapshot artifacts

objectives.text: Understand why webhook delivery, queueing, and worker execution are separate responsibilities.
Understand why snapshot artifacts live in a shared store that both agents and humans can update.

teaches.point: The webhook handler only translates push events into durable jobs, keeping GitHub delivery independent from analysis runtime.
The shared snapshot store is where agent output and future human feedback meet without either Augur or the website claiming exclusive ownership.
